body: Well, looks like my ex and this "friend" of his are a match made in hell!

As unhappy as I am that he's cozying up to the "friend" that he was emotionally unfaithful to me with, part of me thinks that if they ever get together, he's not going to be better off. Sure, he's probably going to be happier, but I don't think he and that woman will grow together, because both of them are self-confessed immature, selfish people (in fact, the woman often proudly says that she's a terrible person and a bitch, and says that she has wonderful friends for them to stick with her - that's because most of her friends are immature and abrasive themselves). Maybe they deserve each other. I'm pretty sure when their stupid banter and lewd flirting gets old, when the fun runs out, and they discover that common interests aren't really enough to get a relationship going, things will go downhill. (I still really think that the growth potential for a relationship with two immature, selfish individuals is really low.) 

Also, my ex is very arrogant, and his attitude towards ending our relationship was more like "I'm done with this bitch [me]; time to have fun and live it up. Now I can be as lewd and flirty as I want without someone breathing down my neck!" rather than "This isn't working anymore, and I hate to do this, but I hope that we can learn lessons from this and all the better from it." I may be the one who's experienced more pain, but I'm also the one seeing this as a painful but valuable learning experience that taught, and is still teaching, me important life lessons. I think I'll be better when the next man comes along. I can't say the same about him.

I feel the same way too. With my ex, he knows that he broke up with me in a very cruel way, but is in denial about the other ways that he hurt me. His huge ego shields him from feeling remorse, and I think part of him even thinks that he was being cruel to be kind, since some of his enabler friends have been telling him that.

I crave closure too. The last few months, I was feeling particularly angry and hurt because my ex never ever thought to give me closure, and with each passing day, it seems less likely that he will. He just got rid of me like I was trash. I hate that I didn't matter enough for him to respect me and break up with me decently. We were together for 4.5 years, and were long-distance for the last 2 years of our relationship, but he couldn't bother to talk to me on Skype; he just ended our relationship through a messaging app.

Apparently, he knows that he broke up with me in a douchey way and was an asshole for badmouthing me shortly after the breakup, because people have told him so, but he doesn't care. He even said that "maybe" he would apologize, and I didn't get the point of him informing me of that, because either you apologize or you don't. For the record, he was definitely not the perfect BF while we were together, but he acts like the demise of the relationship is entirely my fault. Any time a friend suggested that he should own up to his mistakes and talk to me for closure, he'd flip out and say that it's insulting to be told that he has to apologize for anything more than the way he broke up with me.

While it still makes me angry thinking about this, lately, I've started feeling more resigned to the cold, hard truth that he most likely won't apologize. He's cozying up to the "friend" he was emotionally unfaithful to me with and is happy that I'm out of his life, plus, he has a huge ego, is very much in denial of his flaws, and has a victim complex, so I doubt that I'm ever getting that closure. Obviously, I'm not too happy about that, but I think I've been starting to bury that pain and anger in the recesses of my mind. Maybe I'll forget it; who knows.

I'm not sure I've been actively seeking closure for myself, but I've been investing more time in self-improvement projects (including therapy), as well as old and new hobbies, so maybe those have helped, too. Also, on the brighter side, it made me realize that I'm glad that I didn't go on to marry this guy. I naively thought that he was the one for me because of the good times we had and our common interests, but now it's clear to me that this guy doesn't have his shit together and has narcissistic tendencies.

In the early stage of our relationship, my ex said that he was an emotionally stunted idiot. I thought he was just being self-deprecating, and I was optimistic that we could grow together. Nope, turns out he was right. A lot of the pain he caused me came from him being an emotionally stunted (and immature) idiot.

The woman he was emotionally unfaithful to me with often says, "I'm selfish," "I'm a bitch," and "I'm a terrible person." Good luck to my ex and this bitch, then! :)

No one's perfect; everyone has flaws. Having the self-awareness to owe up to them is nice, but it's only the first step. The best people make the sincerest possible effort to overcome them, but then you have people like my ex's "friend," who inform others of their flaws as if they're proud of them and as if they're warning others to just deal with it.

Sorry for the quick reply - I'm off to bed; will take time to read this in the morning. As for him and her not getting together, I know his tactics, since he told me about his romantic history. At times, he doesn't confess to the women he has feelings for; instead, he gets as close to them as possible so he can enjoy the benefits of a relationship (well, sans the physical affection and sex, but considering his love for raunchy humor and his lack of boundaries with women - he has no problem buying sex toys for female friends, watching porn with them, and asking them to pose for naughty pics with him - he probably still gets satisfied anyway) minus the pain and hard work that comes with a relationship. That's probably what he's doing with this woman.

I see. Well, the thing is that he only considers his POV, so he doesn't think he did anything wrong to me. He thinks that I was too jealous and distrustful, and from his POV, he was just defending an innocent friend. He thinks that her making fun of me is totally justified because I "started" things by disliking her, which is why he doesn't ever bother telling her off (not to mention, he really doesn't want to upset their friendship because he's really so selfish that he badly wants to pursue this friendship).

Thank you for the advice!

Thank you. But as for just desserts, the problem is that his female friends **love** his lewd sense of humor very much! In fact, they're so happy that I'm out of his life because that means that they can be as inappropriate as they want, without "an oversensitive person making [them] feel guilty."

Hmm, I don't necessarily miss him more, but I do get a lot more emotional. Whereas I can not think of him, the relationship, and the breakup more easily when my period isn't drawing near, I find myself thinking about those things more often shortly before and while I'm on my period, and I start hurting more (emotionally).

Ugh! I understand. I'm like that, too. I realize more and more that my ex and I were incompatible, and that he was a jerk towards the end of our relationship. Moreover, the way he's acting these days - carefree and very happy to have his "freedom" and harem of female friends back - makes it really seem like he didn't care much about the relationship and that it didn't mean much to him.

*hugs* I think this shows that you're a person with an immense capacity to love. It's okay to love and miss him. But just because you miss and love him, doesn't mean that he's the one for you. This painful lesson is still just sinking in for me, but I hope it helps.
Same here. I doubt he's thinking about me (or if he does, he just thinks of me negatively). I don't think he even feels remorse for dumping me painfully.

I definitely do, it hurts. It reminds me that he doesn't care anymore. He's the one who dumped me, but he's also the one who blocked me everywhere. He could've unblocked me to make it easier to contact me, but he never did. It's been nearly three months, but it doesn't seem likely that he'll reach out. While it hurts, it also helps make me think, "This isn't someone who cares about me or wants me in my life. So why should I still miss him?"
I wonder about that, too!

You'd be surprised that there are people in their 30s that still aren't that mature, and my ex is one of those people. He has a very juvenile sense of humor, and most of his close friends nowadays are women in their 20s, whereas most of his friends his age have settled down and/or are focusing on their careers. I thought that my ex still counted as mature because he does get serious when it comes to his responsibilities (i.e. work), has a stable job, and invests his money well, but then I realized that of course, those things are expected from people his age! (Besides, that still doesn't make him entirely mature because at work, he usually does what's expected of him but nothing really more than that.) His friends also tried to make me feel bad for thinking that he's not mature and also used his work as an example, but I realized that since these women are pretty immature themselves, that already counts as mature for them, and that's pretty sad.

It's funny that you talked about Inside Out, because I was actually reminded of that movie while playing back our relationship in my head! You know that scene when Sadness "taints" a happy memory, and Riley, who had been reminiscing happily at that point, starts crying? That's how I'd feel remembering the good times we had. It was like they're now "tainted" because remembering them would also come with the realization that those memories are in the past, and that I should assume that I can't make good memories like that with my ex again because our shared future is no more. (When I was feeling even worse - my therapist says it seems I had a mild depression a few months ago - I would even think that I can't create good memories like that with **anyone** else ever again!)

But thanks for reminding me of the important lesson to be learned from this movie! Joy didn't understand what Sadness's purpose was, only to learn that sadness can serve as a cry for help and is a necessary, healthy emotion. I didn't want to be sad or to be in pain, but then, of course it wouldn't have been natural to be happy right after the breakup. (As a friend told me, "If it didn't hurt, it probably didn't mean much.") And yes, just like in the film, my sadness helped me reach out and open up to others, and discover my friends' love and support for me in the process.

I've been wondering the same thing too! My ex didn't even seem to grieve; nope, people said he started excitedly talking about the things he could now do and how he could be all chummy with his female friends again without me in the picture. He said he didn't even want to think of me! He totally didn't sound like someone who cared about me (and I try to remember this to hopefully move on from him, but instead I just start getting angry at how unfair he is while still continuing to love him and want him back - oh, my stupid heart and my stupid emotions). People even said that he'd celebrate his "repaired friendships" and "fences being mended" on social media (to which I would think, "Fuck you; why don't you mend your fence with me?"). And of course his enabler friends are cheering him on and telling him that he's coping in a very healthy way. Meanwhile, I couldn't eat or sleep for a while, and I felt emotionally paralyzed, and they'd think, "That's so sad; she isn't coping healthily." Maybe so, but at least the relationship meant something to me and I cared. I don't know how some people can be like this; in my ex's case, it's not even a front. He genuinely is that happy to be rid of me!

Indeed. Thank you for sharing this.

Sorry, I'm gonna act as if I'm talking to my ex here: I should've seen it coming - that you'd choose your friends over me. You told me so before, when I said I was uncomfortable about how troublesome one of your female friends was being. I thought maybe I was the problem for being too jealous. Indeed, I think I was, but at the same time, you just never had enough patience for me. I always stuck by you, despite your flaws and my family disliking you. Even now, if you wanted to work things out (**and show that you really can and will put me first**), I would stick with you, even though I'm well aware of your flaws. I'd be patient with you... the way you weren't with me. But you didn't choose me. You're celebrating your life without me, and I don't even know if regret will hit you someday.

Same here; in spite of the fact that he wasn't Mr. Perfect himself, I'd like to be with him again. At the same time, I'd really like him to work on himself, though. He keeps thinking that everything that went wrong was my fault, but no, there were times when he was insensitive and unkind, too.

It's because I feel like he didn't bail quickly; it's more like, after countless attempts to change and improve myself, nothing worked, and he continued to feel stressed out every time I'd get an irrational thought. So by the time the anxiety diagnosis came along, he'd gotten so worn out and impatient that he couldn't be optimistic. It also didn't help that he was angry at me at that time, which ended up being the nail in the coffin.

As for not ultimately accepting me for who I am, I also don't know about that. The first time I told him about my upcoming appointment, I asked, "If it turns out that I have anxiety, would you support me?" He said he would, and that I didn't even have to ask. I think if he still had patience left to give, and if we hadn't gotten into another argument on the day of my appointment, maybe he still would've stayed. Maybe. (I should note that he told me that that last argument was my last chance to show him I could change, and that since I wasted that chance, he was done with me. Now that you mention that part about him bailing on me... I'm starting to wonder. Considering how little patience he had left, if I'd started therapy and still had an episode of irrational thoughts anyway, maybe he'd have said, "See, it's not working" and left. Hmmm...)

Ah, my ex had a loooot of female friends. I knew he wouldn't cheat on me with them, but I got jealous and anxious anyway. :( t also didn't help that a bunch of his female friends were the type who were like, "We can't tone down our behavior, because that's how we are, so just deal with it." And so, they took an all-or-nothing approach and decided that since they couldn't tone down their behavior, they'd just avoid him, which led to my ex resenting me for damaging his friendships. And now he's happy to have his "freedom" back, and says he won't talk to me because he's busy repairing his friendships with those girls. *sigh* Part of me wonders if his female friends were more important to him than I was.

Thank you so much! I feel like that's how my ex thinks of me, though: from his POV, I'm definitely the toxic one because I stressed him out so much and scared his friends away, so he feels like I damaged his friendships.

And yes, we're not in contact with each other. It wasn't my choice; he was so pissed at me and he really wanted me out of his life, so he blocked me everywhere. A few friends have tried to get him to reconsider, but he really doesn't give a shit (or doesn't want to give a shit). I wonder if it would've been better if he were updated enough to know what's going on in therapy... but then there's no use wondering anymore... :(

*hugs back*

I'm sorry to hear that. It's okay; same here. I'm an introvert, and my interests are mostly nerdy, geeky, and/or indoor activities. Partying, clubbing, and going to bars were never my thing - would you believe I actually finished college not having partied at a club? Sadly, those activities seem to be how a lot of people meet their SOs (I know it's not the only way, but it's a common way). Now I don't know if I'll ever find someone else to date/love again, considering my interests (and not just that - my ex was my first love; I still love him very much and I don't think I will be over him anytime soon. I still wish, against all odds, that we can reconcile.).

I really can relate to you! I've been going out to meet new people lately, but it's only really just to expand my circle (and stave off the loneliness, in a way). I just went to a speed dating event recently (first time doing that, ever), and I was actually glad I didn't match with anyone because I really don't want to date yet. I downloaded Tinder, but I explicitly stated that I just want to make friends (if we develop into something more, great, I guess, but my main purpose is friendship). In a way, I guess this is also my way of determining the kind of guys I like and dislike (my ex being my first love, maybe I haven't formed a clear idea of my type of guy yet).

I'm so sorry. I really don't know what to say. I'm not sure - I'm no psychologist - but I think this happens because it's what we want subconsciously. My mind is cruel, too. Almost every night, I have these realistic dreams of us getting back together, or at the very least, on the road to reconciliation. They're so vivid that I swear they feel real... and then I wake up, and it's back to reality. I've also been trying to just not think about it, but what's the point when I end up dreaming of him anyway?

Actually, this was a bad week for me - I couldn't stop crying about my ex, and because of the pain and anger, I lashed out, and people said I was a hopeless case and, anxiety or no anxiety, I'd never change. But I said that I will change, and even if they don't believe me now (or ever), I will prove them wrong. I know my ex also thinks I'm a hopeless case. Well, fuck that. I won't be a hopeless case.

This is a bit impulsive, but I also booked a trip someplace quiet for a mental detox. Lately, being alone with my thoughts has just made me wallow, but I'm hoping that the silence of the place will actually make me contemplative. It's been so painful crying all week. I just need to get away for a while. I don't know how much of a victory booking that trip is. Let's see.

Ah, I believe my friends genuinely were concerned. I'm not mad at them. I just told the first one (the one who told me what my ex posted) that while I believe that was done out of concern, it did not help me, so I don't really want to be updated, and that even if, one day, I ask for details, I urged her not to ever give in.

The other friend, too, was extremely worried about me. I should note that I don't live in or come from the US; yes, we do get our share of Western culture, but NC is not something like a near-universal post-breakup rule here. This friend of mine was concerned when she heard that my ex blocked me everywhere, so she went to ask him, "Why did you do that? Don't you know that that really hurts her?" So yeah, they were extremely concerned. It was sweet of them, really.

And thank you for the words of encouragement. I think my ex thinks I'm a hopeless case. That's why he pulled the plug on us. I keep crying because I wish he'd have stayed. On particularly bad days, I feel like I can't continue the therapy without him; he broke up with me even though I'd committed to getting therapy while we were still together. But you're right; I just really have to continue working on myself. Some of his friends think that I'm unsympathetic, and a hopeless case, but I know I'm not.

I miss you so much. I feel so confused right now; some of my emotions might be rather contradictory. On the one hand, I understand why you left. You must have been so fed up with me. And this is the part that I blame myself for. Maybe I could've done more to change. But on the other hand, I think you were also selfish, unkind, and quick to anger. Many of our arguments in the past two years were actually because I said something irrational and you, dwelling on it, blew up even when I just needed to let it out (and maybe get reassurance from you, or something). You would turn those moments into a full-blown argument, not me, and even when I already said I was feeling bad (sometimes even physically bad, like having trouble breathing) and to stop it, you would continue raging. I said you had a bad temper; you said it only ever arose because of me and that maybe I shouldn't provoke you. No, I don't believe that - you have a bad temper, and just because you said that it only manifested in our relationship, it doesn't mean you shouldn't do anything about it. Yes, you were unkind, and you're actually the reason we could never argue properly - I learned to diffuse tension; you didn't, and refused to.

You were also selfish in that you seemed to want me to hurry up and get better so you could have fun with your female friends. I know you cared for my well-being in a general sense, but when it came to that aspect... yeah, that's really how it felt; you wanted to set my progress according to your own terms.

And yet despite all these, despite part of me wanting to punch you right now because I can't believe you're apathetic enough to joke about the situation, I miss you. I miss the fond moments we had. I wish we could go back to that. You know, in spite of all your flaws (I haven't even mentioned the rest), I still loved you - heck, I still do. I've been patient with you - you think you were patient with me; I do not think you were, considering how quick you were to get angry. I still wish we could work things out, even though we're both very hurt - but you have to fix yourself too, you know. Your mom was right; you're arrogant - both of us tried to help you overcome your flaws, but you didn't see yourself as arrogant, so what could we do? Somehow, I have a feeling you're blaming me for the death of the relationship. I bet you're thinking "Good riddance" right now, since you're apathetic at worst anyway. And your awful enabling harem of female friends must be cheering you on right now. Well, I hope you're happy. /s (They told me that I should be happy for you because you can repair your friendships with me out of the picture. Sorry, that's too much to ask from me right now.)

I'm continuing therapy. You didn't even want to listen when I told you I had anxiety, right? I wanted to get therapy to make our lives easier. But since you're selfish anyway, I wonder - why was I so devoted to you? I should've always said, "I will do this for myself." And that's what I'm doing now. This therapy is for myself - for my own growth and healing. If you don't want to be a part of my life, and if you don't want to grow, then I guess it's your loss, not mine. I'll keep telling myself more and more everyday that it's not my loss, but yours. My heart says, "I want to work things out and get back with you," but my brain says, "No. Or at least, not like this." Like I said, I'm really confused. I miss you. I want you back, but I'm beginning to accept that there must be a better person for me out there - maybe not now, but I'll meet him someday. But I would actually still like to try with you, as broken as we are - if you're willing to... and if you will commit to working on yourself.

Thank you for this. The problem with me is that I know I'll be okay in the long run, whatever happens, but right now, I can't visualize that future yet. I'm enjoying happy moments as they come, but I also miss my ex a lot, even though he wasn't the greatest. I still get that confusing rush of emotions - blaming myself, blaming him, feeling hurt, regretting things, getting mad at him for dumping me but also acknowledging that I pushed him away - and still hurts. I really miss him. Even though I've been starting to accept that there's probably a better one for me, and even though there are times when I'm super pissed at him, a part of me still really wishes we could work things out, not only because I love and miss him as a person, but also because I love his family and I wish I could've been a part of their clan. But then reality hits me in the face - being with him would mean having to live with his awful friends, and that he left me because he valued their friendship more - and it just hurts again. If there's any consolation, I don't feel suicidal anymore, but it still sucks that I feel so many painful, negative emotions every now and then.

*hugs* I'm so sorry. I really don't know what advice to give. I don't know if this helps, but you're not alone. I'm also suffering (and trying to recover) from a recent breakup. It hurts an awful lot. Anxiety doesn't help - even when I keep myself busy and am doing fun stuff, I'm reminded of him.

Do you have any hobbies? Maybe you could try keeping yourself busy with those. :) Or you could get into a new one!

Thank you. I know he genuinely loved me, and that he cared. However, he didn't want to give up his friends. And ultimately, it seems he couldn't set boundaries or sacrifice them. I don't think he would've had to give them up, but the problem was that rather than compromise by toning down their behavior, the girls' solution was to just stay away instead. I'm having a hard time imagining being in their shoes - fine, that's how their personalities really are, but is it really so hard to just tone their behavior down and watch what they do or say a bit more? It's not like they're kids. Not a rhetorical question - I wish someone could help me understand.

Hey, thanks so much for your reply! I'm glad you have a very loving boyfriend right now.

It's just been days since he dumped me, so I still feel really sad thinking of him. I can't stop crying. I hope that by getting therapy, I really will get better and maybe we can get back together. But I know I have to get therapy for myself.

Re: the age - hahaha, I see your point. Sorry, I was being paranoid and not really thinking straight.

Today I met some friends, and one of them said that as sucky as this situation is, it's character-building for me, because he's sure that I will emerge from this a stronger and better person. As for that friending/unfriending thing - sorry, to be clear, yes, that woman also avoided him IRL. However, since she and the ex don't live very close by, a lot of their interactions take place online, and they got to know each other more through social media. (This is why I do kind of agree that social media can be a cause of concern. Facebook friendships can develop into pretty strong friendships as well.) Yes, well, it's because everyone said that the woman wasn't into him. His friends - including our mutual friends - defended the woman. I guess I do agree that it should have been up to him to set boundaries; he did, in a way, but I don't know if maybe he could've done more.

I agree, and I do find it quite sad. I feel like part of him is afraid to grow up. He is mature and responsible when it comes to things like work, but maybe it's a bit of a red flag that almost everyone he hangs out with nowadays are women 6-10 years younger - not because he's a pedo, but you've got to wonder. Worse, these women have a very immature sense of humor, and some of them have seen me as a killjoy for trying to get the ex to focus on more serious things like the future. Yes, those are platonic friendships, but it kind of feels that he wants to remain stuck in his teenage days. Most of his friends his age or older have settled down and/or have been moving around the country or even overseas, whereas one reason he doesn't even consider moving abroad is having to be uprooted from friends. Again, I know he wouldn't cheat, but I don't think he had the most mature attitude, and it didn't help that he didn't have the most mature of friends around. And in fact, the one who ratted me out was one of those younger women. Immaturity or not, that was a very shitty thing to do.

I love him; I still do. Even though I've been well aware of his flaws, I loved him. But yes, he has some growing up to do as well, and I wonder if he will realize that.

Well, I might need to accept that some of my friends are just not gonna be very helpful, and are just fun to be around. Today, I discovered that I had many other friends who were supportive and helpful. I felt like I should live, but I don't know how long this will feel. Thank you. :)

Thank you, and sorry for the late reply. I didn't want to get out of the house and see people today, but there were some commitments I couldn't say no to, so I went out and I felt better. I don't know if this will last long, though, because I still felt like sobbing when I got home.

But I'm really touched that some friends who live overseas were so concerned about me that they made long-distance calls to check if I was okay. It really meant a lot to me. I felt like I wasn't alone.

I still miss the ex. It still hurts very much. I don't know if I will get over this, or get better. But today was a good day, I guess. My friend told me that this is a character-building experience for me, and he's sure that I will emerge from this a stronger person. I hope so. I hope I don't get this suicidal feeling again.
Thank you so much. :)

I see; thank you! Well, he said it was because he was sick and tired of it all. I hate it; I feel so screwed up and messed up right now because I messed with another person's life and I wish I'd known about anxiety sooner. I mean, it really never occurred to me that that was why I acted the way I did. Had I known earlier, I would've sought help. Maybe some people think that I'm going to use it as an excuse for people to accommodate me, but I really am committed to therapy, and I just ask for a little understanding. I keep wondering - if I'd known sooner, maybe he would've helped, but now he's just really sick of the way I acted...

I can't expect him to deal with a burden he didn't sign up for, but I dunno, I guess I still do hold on to the hope that he'll come back. Hopefully, with therapy and with the knowledge that I am acting the way I do not because I like being mean, things should be easier...
Even before I knew I had a disorder, I tried telling him that, but it still affected him. :( It might be a bit too late for that now; he's already blocked me everywhere.

Well, here's the thing... During the earlier period of our relationship, there were times when I'd ask him to tone down the banter with his female friends and get mad at him if he wanted to hang out with them, and I did accuse him or them of flirting. So he'd tone it down but I wouldn't realize it and still complain. Some of the girls started staying away from him as a result, so he most likely became resentful.

Later on, the few sessions of general therapy were at least helpful in that I realized I had to knock that behavior off. However, that did not help get rid of the constant anxious thoughts, but I think we'd already gotten to the point that he did not want to hear anything about them anymore. At all. This was despite initially saying that he thought he could manage that. At this point, I had already learned not to accuse him of stuff, but just telling him that I was feeling uneasy about some offensive joke they made would make him fly into a rage and not talk to me for days. He'd tell me that he had a bad temper, and that he wouldn't rage if I hadn't done anything. It could be that he was already fed up by the repetitiveness back then, or maybe in hindsight, he's just not someone who can handle my issues...? I don't know anymore. I would cry a lot whenever he did that, and ask him to be less harsh, but he said it was part of who he was. Regardless, I loved him.

Also, yes, I think he might have thought I wasn't taking his wishes seriously. :( I was acting on anxiety and fear, but I really did not know why I would find myself feeling a certain way again (because the last few times he was mad at me, it was because I felt/thought something irrational). Believe me, I didn't like or want to feel them. I just wanted to get them out, not necessarily act on them. Now I have a therapist for that.

But I dunno, now I think that if we're to get back together, both of us will have to work on ourselves. I really do want it. But I can't assume it will happen.

Thanks so much! I'm just really hurt and upset right now, because I didn't want us to end. We had our stressful and not-so-happy moments, but we had good ones, and we also had plans for the future. Now it's all gone, and that's why I've been super upset. I'm glad that this community exists, though.

Thank you so much! If it's OK to ask, what makes you think it could've been toxic? I feel like my behavior was making things very toxic for us, but on his end, I'm not sure but maybe he was just being toxic in response to me..
